item.title: Police investigate death of 12-year-old boy in Wailoku, man in custody
item.description: Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the death of a 12-year-old boy in Wailoku, with a 29-year-old man in custody in relation to the incident. Police say the boy was last seen playing at a neighbour's home on Wednesday evening but did not return home.
item.content:encoded:
Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the death of a 12-year-old boy in Wailoku, with a 29-year-old man in custody in relation to the incident.

Police say the boy was last seen playing at a neighbour's home on Wednesday evening but did not return home.

They say his mother later reported him missing.

Police say his body was discovered near his home at around midday yesterday.

item.title: Fijian conjoined twins reach Saudi Arabia for possible separation surgery
item.description: The Ministry of Health says the twins' family had searched for treatment overseas, but surgery costing more than US$1 million was beyond their reach. They say the family was later accepted into the Saudi Conjoined Twins Programme, which is fully funded by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and covers all medical treatment, travel and accommodation costs for the twins and their family.
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Health says the twins' family had searched for treatment overseas, but surgery costing more than US$1 million was beyond their reach.

They say the family was later accepted into the Saudi Conjoined Twins Programme, which is fully funded by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and covers all medical treatment, travel and accommodation costs for the twins and their family.

The sisters, who are from Nausori, were born as part of an extremely rare set of triplets and are joined at the chest, abdomen and pelvis. Their condition is one of only two publicly recorded cases of conjoined twins in Fiji over the past 50 years.

item.title: Social welfare payments to continue despite end of Insurance Scheme
item.description: The Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection says the change only affects the insurance scheme, which provided one-off financial assistance for funeral expenses, fire losses and accident-related claims. Acting Permanent Secretary Selina Kuruleta says the Government has allocated about $184 million to continue supporting people through its existing social welfare programmes.
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection says the change only affects the insurance scheme, which provided one-off financial assistance for funeral expenses, fire losses and accident-related claims.

Acting Permanent Secretary Selina Kuruleta says the Government has allocated about $184 million to continue supporting people through its existing social welfare programmes.

She says payments under the Family Assistance Scheme, Child Protection Allowance, Disability Allowance Scheme, Social Pension Scheme, Transport Assistance Programme and the Allowance for Rural Pregnant Mothers will continue as normal.

Kuruleta acknowledges that the end of the insurance scheme may cause concern for some families, but says the Government remains committed to supporting those most in need through its existing social protection programmes.

She adds that healthcare-related assistance will also continue through the Ministry of Health and other government agencies.

People seeking more information are encouraged to visit their nearest Social Welfare office or call the Ministry's toll-free line on 1561.

item.title: More than 1,000 people in Nalawa to receive electricity through new project
item.description: The Nalawa Stage 2 Grid Extension and Rural Electrification Project extends electricity from Nasau Village to Nukuilau Village, supplying power to Ovalau Village, Nasau Primary School and the Nasau Health Centre. Speaking at the commissioning of the project, Minister for Public Works, Ro Filipe Tuisawau says house wiring worth about $435,000 will also be carried out for 267 households, benefiting
item.content:encoded:
The Nalawa Stage 2 Grid Extension and Rural Electrification Project extends electricity from Nasau Village to Nukuilau Village, supplying power to Ovalau Village, Nasau Primary School and the Nasau Health Centre.

Speaking at the commissioning of the project, Minister for Public Works, Ro Filipe Tuisawau says house wiring worth about $435,000 will also be carried out for 267 households, benefiting an estimated 1,068 people.

He says while some house wiring work is still outstanding, it is expected to be completed by December.

Tuisawau says the Government fully funded the project at a cost of about $2.45 million, meaning communities are no longer required to contribute towards rural electrification projects, as they did in the past.

He says reliable electricity will improve daily life for families while also supporting better learning opportunities for students, enhancing services at the local health centre and creating opportunities for businesses to grow.

The Minister says the Government remains committed to ensuring every Fijian has access to electricity by 2030 and has already connected more than 30,000 households through its rural electrification programme.

item.title: Style Fiji aims to double funds raised for charity tonight
item.description: Style Fiji organisers are aiming to double the funds raised for charity this year as they prepare to launch the 2026 edition of Fiji's largest charity fashion and entertainment event. Speaking ahead of the Style Fiji 2026 launch, which will take place this evening at the Sheraton Fiji Golf & Beach Resort in Denarau, Nadi, committee member Samson Lee highlighted that the event will provide sponsors
item.content:encoded:
Style Fiji organisers are aiming to double the funds raised for charity this year as they prepare to launch the 2026 edition of Fiji's largest charity fashion and entertainment event.

Speaking ahead of the Style Fiji 2026 launch, which will take place this evening at the Sheraton Fiji Golf & Beach Resort in Denarau, Nadi, committee member Samson Lee highlighted that the event will provide sponsors and supporters with greater transparency on how funds are used while unveiling this year's theme and charity beneficiaries.

Style Fiji is an annual charity fashion and entertainment event that raises funds for local health and community organisations, including the Fiji Cancer Society and the Spinal Injury Association of Fiji.

Lee says the launch has been organised primarily for sponsors, major supporters and long-time guests, with around 100 to 130 people expected to attend.

He says the evening will provide a breakdown of how last year's funds were spent, introduce the committee's chosen charities for 2026, and allow guests to pre-purchase tables and tickets for the main event .

Lee says this year's launch marks a new direction for Style Fiji, as last year's gathering focused mainly on the transition following the handover of the event.

He says the charity event is now in its 15th year and has continued to be held at the Sheraton Fiji Golf & Beach Resort after moving from Sofitel Fiji Resort & Spa to provide more space and improved parking for guests.

He says although Style Fiji is known for its glamorous fashion showcase, its heart has always been charity.

Lee says last year's event raised $50,000 , and the committee's goal this year is to double that amount .

He says launching the campaign earlier will help build excitement, strengthen support and give sponsors more time to get involved.

Lee adds that tonight's event will also provide an opportunity for sponsors, business leaders, tourism industry representatives and influencers to network while learning more about the committee's plans for the 2026 event.

item.title: Fijians to pay less for fuel but more for gas from today
item.description: Fijians will pay less for fuel from today, with diesel recording the biggest price drop, while households using liquefied petroleum gas (LPG ) will pay slightly more. The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission has announced the new regulated fuel and LPG prices, which come into effect today following its monthly review of international refined fuel prices, the Butane Contract Price, freight ra
item.content:encoded:
Fijians will pay less for fuel from today, with diesel recording the biggest price drop, while households using liquefied petroleum gas (LPG ) will pay slightly more.

The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission has announced the new regulated fuel and LPG prices, which come into effect today following its monthly review of international refined fuel prices, the Butane Contract Price, freight rates and foreign exchange movements for imports during June 2026.

The price of diesel will decrease by 47 cents per litre from $3.39 to $2.92 , in areas of Viti Levu located within 3 kilometres of any public road.

Unleaded fuel will decrease by 38 cents , from $3.44 to $3.06 per litre .

Premix will decrease by 34 cents , from $3.27 to $2.93 per litre , while kerosene will decrease by 37 cents , from $2.71 to $2.34 per litre .

Meanwhile, LPG prices will increase across all categories.

The price of a 4.5kg gas cylinder will increase by 43 cents , from $17.17 to $17.60 , while a 12kg cylinder will increase by $1.12 , from $45.80 to $46.92 .

Bulk LPG will increase by 9 cents per kilogram , from $3.53 to $3.62 , while autogas will increase by 7 cents per litre from $2.43 to $2.49 .

The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission says while international fuel prices eased during the review period, global energy markets remain highly volatile due to geopolitical tensions, changing trade conditions and supply chain disruptions, meaning fuel prices could still move up or down in the coming months.

FCCC Chief Executive Officer Senikavika Jiuta says although the lower fuel prices are welcome news for consumers and businesses, they reflect market conditions during the review period and should not be seen as a sign that prices will continue to fall.

Jiuta says international petroleum markets remain highly sensitive to geopolitical developments, supply disruptions and freight costs.

She says the FCCC will continue to closely monitor these factors to ensure any increase or decrease in international costs is appropriately reflected in Fiji's regulated fuel prices.

item.title: Public urged to verify tax certificates amid fraud alert
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 31/07/2026 Members of the public, businesses, government ministries and departments, statutory bodies, financial institutions, and procurement entities are being urged to exercise extreme caution after the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) detected fraudulent Tax Clearance and Tax Compliance Certificates (TCCs), as well as fake letters falsely claiming that legi
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 31/07/2026

Members of the public, businesses, government ministries and departments, statutory bodies, financial institutions, and procurement entities are being urged to exercise extreme caution after the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) detected fraudulent Tax Clearance and Tax Compliance Certificates (TCCs), as well as fake letters falsely claiming that legitimately issued certificates had been cancelled due to a system error, circulating in the country.

FRCS says the documents are fraudulent, unauthorized, and do not originate from the Service.

The Service warns that the creation, distribution, possession, use, or presentation of false tax documents may constitute serious criminal offences and could result in investigation and prosecution under Fiji's laws, with offenders facing substantial fines, imprisonment, or both.

FRCS says it wishes to clarify that it does not cancel, revoke, or invalidate Tax Clearance or Tax Compliance Certificates through informal emails, third-party correspondence, or unverified letters.

The Service adds that any change to the status of a certificate is reflected through its official systems and can be verified via the FRCS Taxpayer Online Services Certificate Validation Portal.

FRCS Chief Executive Officer Udit Singh says the Service takes any attempt to undermine the integrity of Fiji's tax administration system very seriously.

He says the circulation of fake tax certificates and fraudulent cancellation notices is a deliberate attempt to deceive businesses, government agencies, and the public.

Singh says FRCS will not tolerate any activity that compromises the integrity of its systems and processes.

He stresses the importance of verifying certificates through official channels before accepting them as valid and strongly urges all organisations and individuals not to accept any tax certificate at face value.

Singh adds that verification should be undertaken immediately through the official certificate validation portal or directly with FRCS.

He is advising organisations that if they encounter suspicious certificates, they should take immediate precautionary measures.

Singh says where a fraudulent or suspicious certificate is identified, organisations should retain a copy of the document, suspend the relevant transaction or process, and report the matter immediately to FRCS, together with details of the individual or entity that submitted the document.

He warns that those involved in producing, distributing, possessing, or using fraudulent tax documents could face significant legal consequences.

The CEO says any person found producing, distributing, possessing, or using fraudulent tax documents will be subject to investigation and appropriate action under the law.

Singh says these activities may constitute serious criminal offences, and FRCS will work closely with relevant enforcement agencies to ensure those responsible are held accountable.

FRCS encourages anyone who receives a suspicious certificate, cancellation notice, or related correspondence to report the matter immediately.
